facts.big: is made of · is made in
facts.label: Passivo presente
facts.sub: Use is/are made of para o material e is/are made in para o lugar: The bag is made of leather. It is made in Italy.

facts.label: Material
facts.sub: Para dizer o material, use is/are made of: The bag is made of leather. The shirts are made of cotton. Para perguntar, use What is it made of?

facts.label: Lugar
facts.sub: Para dizer o lugar, use is/are made in: The clock is made in Germany. Para perguntar, use Where is it made? A resposta dá o país.

compare.br: No Brasil, dizemos “feito de couro” e “feito na Itália”.
compare.us: Em inglês: made of + material e made in + lugar. Diga It is made of leather. It is made in Italy.

solo: Peça uma experiência pessoal do aluno com essa diferença.
group: Leia as duas colunas e peça que apontem a maior diferença.
Pergunta: It is made of leather.
extra90: Dupla: um fala como no Brasil, o outro como nos EUA.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.why: We say It is made of wool.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: Made of tells the material. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
Made in tells the place. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
We say “It made of wool”. → Falso (We say It is made of wool.)

pages.title: A gift shop · 1/3
paragraphs: It is Saturday morning in a gift shop in Belfast. Bags, scarves and clocks fill the shelves. Leo walks in and looks around. Blake stands behind the counter. He holds a brown leather bag. He asks Leo a question.
“Hi, Leo! Do you like this bag?” says Blake. “Yes! What is it made of?” says Leo. “It’s made of leather. It’s made in Italy.” says Blake.
